operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are mixed-case with underscores (Ref_Document_Types, Document_Drafts); must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
All tables tiny (3-15 rows); no huge-table sampling path exercised here.
Declared DATETIME (receipt_date, mailing_date) dispatches to Date fuzzer (contains 'date'); storage is text with format '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' (datetime, not date-only).
Date fuzzer template detection: samples like '2008-04-21 20:42:25' parse under a datetime template; leading-zero stripping rule may fire since values contain '-0'.
CHAR(15) columns dispatch to String(length=15); VARCHAR(255) to String(length=255); both text storage.
INTEGER columns dispatch to Number(scale=0, is_int=True); storage integer; samples are small ints (0..20).

Composite FK: Draft_Copies(document_id,draft_number)->Document_Drafts; Circulation_History(document_id,draft_number,copy_number)->Draft_Copies. Upstream fk dict is per-column, so composite FK is split into independent per-column edges (loses tuple correlation).
Circulation_History has 3 separate FK edges to Draft_Copies (document_id, draft_number, copy_number) each independently filled -> tuple may not exist in parent.
Documents.shipping_agent_code is nullable FK (notnull=0) but null_rate 0.0 in original; TS may emit NULLs there.
All FKs have existing parents; no dangling/self FKs. No unique/check constraints beyond PKs.
Ref_Document_Types.document_type_code samples include 'Hard Drive' (spaced value) though CHAR(15) code column; description values are single chars ('b','u','f').
operator_ts_expectations: String fuzzer for all CHAR/VARCHAR: fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with contamination, plus literal-pool values; names/descriptions become gibberish -> FN on queries filtering real names (e.g. shipping_agent_name='UPS').

Number fuzzer for INTEGER PKs: fresh ints in [-1,1] range (scale 0) perturbed +-1/+-2, plus pool values; document_id/employee_id/address_id become tiny/negative -> joins still work but range predicates (id>N) shift.

Date fuzzer for DATETIME: template from first parsable sample (datetime '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'), range from min/max parsed; fresh dates uniform in [1973,2014] -> plausible, but format may drop leading zeros -> string comparisons on dates can FP/FN.

FK columns filled from parent's final values with replacement -> many-to-one ties preserved; but composite FKs split per-column -> Draft_Copies/Circulation_History tuples may not match parent tuples -> join FN.
PK dedup keeps first occurrence; composite PKs (document_id,draft_number) dedup on tuple -> draft_number ties across documents preserved.
Small parent tables (3-5 rows) with replacement -> heavy duplicate FK values, plausible for many-to-one but may over-represent one parent.
Literal pool from train SQL seeds real codes ('CD','Paper','working','done','UPS') into String samplers -> some queries match; others miss.
Number PKs fresh-drawn independently of FK children -> child document_id may reference non-existent Documents row (FK not enforced, pragma off) -> join FN.
String length range from elements: single-char descriptions ('b','u') give length range [1,2] -> very short fresh strings, unlike 255-char VARCHAR intent.
Date fuzzer p-inversion: p=0.2 means element returned w.p. 0.2, fresh w.p. 0.8 -> mostly fresh dates, few real ones.
Empty-string / NULL: notnull columns not enforced in Python; insert failures skipped -> some rows dropped silently, shrinking tables.
Boolean/bit/year fuzzers unused here (no such declared types).
